title: Derived naturality, shifts and site comparison for local-class edges
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Work with ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A$ on the small etale and pro-etale sites and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $D^+$ for objects with cohomology vanishing sufficiently far below. Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\tau\in\{\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}\}$, and let $V\in D^+(T_\tau,A)$. Use cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and derived sections at site objects. For each integer $r$, sheafification of $W\mapsto H^r(W,V)$ is canonically $\mathcal H^r(V)$. Its map at the final object defines
$$e_V^r:H^r(T_\tau,V)\longrightarrow\Gamma(T_\tau,\mathcal H^r(V)),$$
which sends a global class to its local classes. For every derived morphism $f:V\to V'$ one has
$$e_{V'}^r\circ H^r(T_\tau,f)=\Gamma(T_\tau,\mathcal H^r(f))\circ e_V^r.$$
Under the canonical cochain shift identifications, $e_{V[1]}^r=e_V^{r+1}$.

For $V\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $c_V^r:H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},V)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\nu_T^*V)$ be the comparison induced by the derived comparison unit of [sk-prop-sf-comparison]. Under exact inverse image $\mathcal H^r(\nu_T^*V)=\nu_T^*\mathcal H^r(V)$, for every $x$ one has
$$e_{\nu_T^*V}^r(c_V^r(x))=\nu_T^*(e_V^r(x)),$$
where the right side is pullback of the sheaf section using the identification of constant coefficient sheaves. The comparison $c_V^r$ is natural for derived morphisms and compatible with shifts, and the displayed square remains compatible with these operations. No concentration in a single degree or constructibility is required.

proof.text: Use the fully faithful underlying-presheaf functor and exact sheafification. Its right derived functor remains fully faithful, so the derived sheafification counit is invertible. Exact sheafification commutes with cohomology, proving invertibility of the specified sheafification map.

For an exact adjunction, construct the left-homology map data of the adjunct of a short-complex map by transposing its cycle and homology maps. Naturality of the hom bijections verifies the three homology-map equations. The homology comparisons thus preserve adjuncts. Apply this to the ordinary counit, then use the defining derived-counit factorization and localization natural-transformation extensionality. This identifies the edge of an exact right adjoint with its canonical right-derived/exact comparison followed by the inverse cohomology comparison.

The edge for a composite adjunction is the first edge followed by the image of the second edge and the ordinary right-adjoint comparison. Transpose this equality. The canonical composition of right derived functors is conjugate to the exact-left composition comparison, and cohomology comparisons commute with exact composition and natural isomorphisms. Apply the result to constant presheaves, sheafification, and terminal evaluation. The exact-adjoint calculation of Step 2 identifies precisely localClassTerminalCohomologyIso and the evaluated presheaf map.

Transpose the edge naturality square. Naturality of the exact-left cohomology comparison and of the derived counit prove it. For shifts use the corresponding shift equation for the exact-left cohomology comparison and the derived counit; the canonical derived adjunction commutes with the fixed shifts.

Compare the bounded and unbounded derived units: their components on images of bounded-below homotopy objects coincide by the two derived-unit factorization equations and rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. Localization extensionality gives equality on all bounded-below derived objects. Consequently boundedBelowComparisonGlobalSections is the restriction of derived etale global sections of the unbounded comparison unit followed by the specified Leray isomorphism.

Apply the composition identity of Step 3 to the comparison adjunction and the etale constant/global-sections adjunction. Edge naturality moves the derived unit through the first edge. The derived triangle identity identifies cohomology of that unit followed by its edge with the ordinary unit followed by exact-inverse-image cohomology comparison. This is exactly localClassSectionPullback. Invertibility of the cohomology comparison follows from boundedBelowComparison.

Naturality of comparison is functoriality of cohomology applied to the natural transformation boundedBelowComparisonGlobalSections. Its unbounded unit-Leray presentation commutes with shifts: each derived adjunction and the canonical right-derived composition comparison commute with shifts. Apply cohomology shift naturality and include the canonical D+ inclusion shift comparison.
